requiredFindings.title: Selection payload shape is unchecked; a malformed selection silently drops or narrows a declared frame
requiredFindings.location: render.py Renderer.run protocol loop (payload.get('alternatives', ...)) and validate_layout
requiredFindings.detail: Frame payloads that are selections are only walked for scalar rules; their layout is never checked. An empty alternatives map yields zero variants and zero TS rows for a frameType that the header enum and frame table still declare, so the carrier cannot represent a declared frame. The frame-table binding added in delta02 is meant to prevent exactly this header/table mismatch. A one-entry map, a missing or unknown select, and extra keys are also accepted. The declared grammar (meta schema 'selection') requires select in {negotiated-target-attribution-v2, host-phase} and exactly two alternatives with no additional properties.
evidence: Ts2 FactBatch payload alternatives = {}: render ok; Ts2FrameV2 TS union has 0 FactBatch rows; by code, the enumerate over empty alternatives emits no Rust payload variant either
alternatives with one entry: render ok, 1 FactBatch row
select deleted: render ok; select 'bogus': render ok; extra key on selection: render ok

test_render.py test_all_frame_payload_positions_use_scalar_validation builds selections with key 'selector' rather than declared 'select'; its refusals come from the scalar walk, so no test checks selection shape
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Recognize a payload as a selection only when it has no 't' key and its keys are exactly {select, alternatives}; require select in the declared enum and exactly two alternatives, each a type; refuse anything else. Fix the test to use 'select' and add refusal tests for empty/one/three alternatives, missing/unknown select and extra keys.

advisories.title: Extern generatedType and names are emitted into code unvalidated
advisories.detail: An extern generatedType 'Foo>); pub fn evil() {} //' renders into both wire.rs and wire.ts. Member names such as 'a-b' render as invalid Rust identifiers, and frameType strings are not pattern-checked. The closed IDL profile/generator closure must validate generatedType against the meta pattern and the actual extern export set, and member/frame names against their patterns. No malicious-IDL claim is made, so this is an advisory, but it matters for integration.

advisories.title: Type objects are not closed
advisories.detail: Unknown or typo keys are ignored: text with 'enumm' renders unconstrained String, uint64 with 'maxx' renders, bytes without minBytes/maxBytes renders. Ts2 frame direction values are not checked (no header member). A non-string text const fails with TypeError instead of ValueError (fails closed). Expected to be covered by the pending closed profile; alternatively, check allowed keys per operator in the renderer.

advisories.title: Redundant nullability forms accepted
advisories.detail: nullable(nullable(T)) renders Option<Option<T>> / ((T) | null) | null, and nullable(null) renders Option<()>. JSON cannot reach Some(None) or Some(()); semantics equal nullable(T)/null, but the representation is ambiguous. Refuse or canonicalize.

advisories.title: Frame payload may reference its own envelope
advisories.detail: A payload ref to Ts2FrameV2 renders Hello(Box<Ts2FrameV2>). Schema-valid and not in the current input; consider refusing envelope refs in payload positions.

advisories.title: Codec duties restated
advisories.detail: Tagged readers require visit_u64 (serde forwards visit_u8/u16/u32) and visit_unit, and accept visit_char as text. Flat serde records still accept bstr for String and bstr/u64-index keys under non-hinting deserializers. Text/bytes length is unbounded before kind check. All disclosed as dedicated-codec duties.

advisories.title: Carried disclosed limits and cosmetics
advisories.detail: Rust frame struct fields are uncorrelated. Derived tagged Serialize emits the tag first and is not qualified CBOR. Consts are inert in Rust. In type-probes.ts the variable 'seal' holds a Rust3DependencySourceChunkV3; renaming it would avoid confusion.
